question: How does Mark begin his Gospel?
answer_choice_2: With the birth of Jesus
answer_choice_3: With “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God”
correct_answer: With “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God”
learning_objective: Recall how Mark opens his account.
explanation: Mark skips birth narratives and opens by declaring Jesus’ identity: Christ, Son of God.
common_misconception: Some expect every Gospel to begin like Matthew or Luke with a birth story.

question: Who baptized Jesus?
answer_choice_2: John the Baptist
correct_answer: John the Baptist
explanation: Jesus came from Nazareth and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
common_misconception: Some confuse John the Baptist with the apostle John.

question: What did the four friends do to get the paralytic to Jesus?
answer_choice_2: Lowered him through the roof
correct_answer: Lowered him through the roof
learning_objective: Recall the determined faith of the paralytic’s friends.
explanation: The crowd blocked the door, so they dug through the roof and lowered the bed.
common_misconception: The detail shows active faith, not mere curiosity.

question: Whom did Jesus say He came to call?
answer_choice_2: The religious leaders
correct_answer: Sinners
explanation: Eating with tax collectors, Jesus said the sick need a physician — He came to call sinners.
common_misconception: Some think Jesus sought out the already-righteous.

question: What happened when Jesus came up out of the baptismal water?
answer_choice_2: The heavens were torn open and the Spirit descended like a dove
correct_answer: The heavens were torn open and the Spirit descended like a dove
learning_objective: Recognize the divine affirmation at the baptism.
explanation: The Spirit descended and the Father declared, “You are my beloved Son.”
common_misconception: All three persons of the Trinity appear in the scene together.

question: What were Simon and Andrew doing when Jesus called them?
answer_choice_2: Casting a net into the sea
correct_answer: Casting a net into the sea
learning_objective: Recall the call of the first disciples.
explanation: Jesus called working fishermen to become fishers of men — and they immediately followed.
common_misconception: They were at work, not at worship, when called.

question: Why did Jesus rise very early and go to a desolate place?
answer_choice_2: To pray
correct_answer: To pray
explanation: Amid intense ministry demand, Jesus withdrew to pray before the day began.
common_misconception: His withdrawal was for communion with the Father, not avoidance of people.

question: What claim scandalized the scribes at the healing of the paralytic?
answer_choice_1: That Jesus could heal on the Sabbath
answer_choice_2: That Jesus could forgive sins
answer_choice_4: That Jesus would rebuild the temple
correct_answer: That Jesus could forgive sins
learning_objective: Connect the healing to Jesus’ authority to forgive.
explanation: “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” — Jesus healed to show the Son of Man’s authority to forgive.
common_misconception: The miracle served the greater claim; forgiveness was the point.

question: How does Isaiah 40:3 frame John the Baptist’s ministry?
answer_choice_1: As a call to rebuild the temple
answer_choice_2: As a voice preparing the way of the Lord
answer_choice_3: As a promise of military victory
answer_choice_4: As a rebuke of Israel’s kings
correct_answer: As a voice preparing the way of the Lord
learning_objective: Connect Mark’s opening citation to its OT context.
explanation: Isaiah’s herald prepares the way for the LORD Himself — Mark applies it to Jesus’ coming.
common_misconception: The citation quietly identifies Jesus with the coming of God, not merely a prophet.

question: At the baptism, “You are my beloved Son” echoes which Old Testament passage?
answer_choice_2: Psalm 2
correct_answer: Psalm 2
learning_objective: Hear the royal-messianic echo in the Father’s words.
explanation: Psalm 2 is God’s enthronement word to His anointed King — the baptism declares Jesus that King.
common_misconception: The words are royal installation language, not only affection.

question: What does “the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath” teach?
answer_choice_2: God’s gifts serve people, and the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath
answer_choice_4: Only priests may interpret the law
correct_answer: God’s gifts serve people, and the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath
learning_objective: Grasp Jesus’ authority over the Sabbath.
explanation: The Sabbath is God’s gift for human good, and Jesus has authority over its meaning.
common_misconception: Jesus was not abolishing rest but exposing legalism.

question: Why does Mark repeatedly say “immediately” in chapter 1?
answer_choice_2: To portray the Servant-King acting with urgency as the kingdom breaks in
correct_answer: To portray the Servant-King acting with urgency as the kingdom breaks in
explanation: Mark’s style presents Jesus in constant, urgent action — the Servant at work.
common_misconception: The pace is a theological portrait, not careless writing.

question: What did Jesus do in the synagogue that led leaders to plot against Him?
answer_choice_2: Healed a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath
correct_answer: Healed a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath
learning_objective: Recall the Sabbath healing and its cost.
explanation: Jesus healed on the Sabbath; Pharisees and Herodians began plotting to destroy Him.
common_misconception: Doing good on the Sabbath was the issue, not breaking God’s law.

question: How many apostles did Jesus appoint on the mountain?
answer_choice_2: Ten
correct_answer: Twelve
learning_objective: Recall the appointing of the twelve.
explanation: Jesus appointed twelve to be with Him and to be sent out to preach.
common_misconception: Being “with Him” came before being sent.

question: In the parable of the sower, what is the seed?
answer_choice_2: The word
correct_answer: The word
explanation: “The sower sows the word” — the soils are responses to it.
common_misconception: The variable is the soil, not the seed.

question: What did Jesus say to the wind and sea?
answer_choice_2: “Peace! Be still!”
correct_answer: “Peace! Be still!”
learning_objective: Recall Jesus’ command over the storm.
explanation: Jesus rebuked the wind and spoke to the sea, and there was a great calm.
common_misconception: He commanded creation directly — no prayer for rescue was needed.

question: What did Jesus’ family say about Him when crowds pressed in?
answer_choice_2: “He is out of his mind”
correct_answer: “He is out of his mind”
learning_objective: See that even Jesus’ family misunderstood Him.
explanation: His family went to seize Him, saying He was out of His mind.
common_misconception: Misunderstanding came even from those closest to Him.

question: By whose power did the scribes claim Jesus cast out demons?
answer_choice_2: Beelzebul’s
correct_answer: Beelzebul’s
explanation: They attributed His exorcisms to the prince of demons; Jesus answered that a divided house cannot stand.
common_misconception: The charge was not that He failed, but that His power was evil.

question: Who did Jesus say is His brother and sister and mother?
answer_choice_2: The twelve only
answer_choice_3: Whoever does the will of God
correct_answer: Whoever does the will of God
explanation: Looking at those seated around Him, Jesus defined His family by obedience to God.
common_misconception: Belonging is defined by doing God’s will, not lineage.

question: What does the saying about the lamp and the basket teach?
answer_choice_2: What is hidden is meant to come to light
correct_answer: What is hidden is meant to come to light
learning_objective: Interpret the lamp saying within the parable section.
explanation: The kingdom’s present hiddenness is temporary — the word is meant to shine.
common_misconception: The saying is about the kingdom’s disclosure, not household advice.

question: Why does Jesus cite Isaiah 6 to explain speaking in parables?
answer_choice_2: Because parables reveal truth to the responsive and conceal it from the hardened
correct_answer: Because parables reveal truth to the responsive and conceal it from the hardened
learning_objective: Understand the dual function of parables.
explanation: Like Isaiah’s ministry, parables both disclose and judge, exposing the hearers’ hearts.
common_misconception: Parables are not simple illustrations; they divide hearers.

question: What does the parable of the seed growing secretly teach about the kingdom?
answer_choice_2: It grows by God’s power even while the farmer sleeps
answer_choice_3: It grows only in good times
correct_answer: It grows by God’s power even while the farmer sleeps
learning_objective: Trust God’s hidden work in kingdom growth.
explanation: The earth produces “by itself” — growth is God’s doing from sowing to harvest.
common_misconception: Faithful sowing matters, but the power is God’s, not ours.

question: What is the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit in its context?
answer_choice_2: Persistently attributing the Spirit’s work in Jesus to Satan
correct_answer: Persistently attributing the Spirit’s work in Jesus to Satan
learning_objective: Read the warning in its narrative context.
explanation: Mark ties the saying to the scribes’ claim that Jesus had an unclean spirit — a settled, hardened rejection.
common_misconception: A believer anxious about this sin shows the very sensitivity that hardened rejection lacks.

question: How does Psalm 107:23-30 deepen the disciples’ question, “Who then is this?”
answer_choice_2: It says the LORD stills storms — Jesus does what only God does
answer_choice_3: It promises calm seas to sailors
correct_answer: It says the LORD stills storms — Jesus does what only God does
learning_objective: Connect the stilled storm to God’s own power.
explanation: In the psalm, sailors cry to the LORD who makes the storm be still; Mark shows Jesus in that role.
common_misconception: The miracle is a claim about Jesus’ identity, not just His compassion.

question: Where did the man with the unclean spirit live?
answer_choice_2: Among the tombs
correct_answer: Among the tombs
explanation: No one could bind him; night and day he cried out among the tombs.
common_misconception: His restoration — clothed and in his right mind — is the point of the scene.

question: Who was healed by touching Jesus’ garment?
answer_choice_2: A woman with a twelve-year discharge of blood
correct_answer: A woman with a twelve-year discharge of blood
learning_objective: Recall the woman healed in the crowd.
explanation: After twelve years and many physicians, she touched His garment and was healed.
common_misconception: Jesus insisted on meeting her personally — faith, not magic, healed her.

question: What did Jesus say to Jairus’s daughter?
answer_choice_2: “Talitha cumi” — “Little girl, arise”
correct_answer: “Talitha cumi” — “Little girl, arise”
learning_objective: Recall the raising of Jairus’s daughter.
explanation: Mark preserves Jesus’ Aramaic words as He raised the twelve-year-old girl.
common_misconception: Jesus treated death as sleep He could wake.

question: How much food did the disciples find for the five thousand?
answer_choice_2: Five loaves and two fish
correct_answer: Five loaves and two fish
learning_objective: Recall the feeding of the five thousand.
explanation: From five loaves and two fish, all ate and were satisfied, with twelve baskets left.
common_misconception: The leftovers exceeded the starting supply.

question: What did Jesus tell Jairus when news came that his daughter had died?
answer_choice_2: “Do not fear, only believe”
correct_answer: “Do not fear, only believe”
learning_objective: Hear Jesus’ word to a grieving father.
explanation: Overhearing the report, Jesus called Jairus past fear into faith.
common_misconception: Faith was called for after hope seemed gone.

question: Why could Jesus do no mighty work in His hometown?
answer_choice_2: Their unbelief
correct_answer: Their unbelief
explanation: He marveled at their unbelief; familiarity bred contempt — “Is not this the carpenter?”
common_misconception: The limit lay in their rejection, not in His power.

question: How did John the Baptist die?
answer_choice_2: Beheaded by Herod after a rash oath
correct_answer: Beheaded by Herod after a rash oath
explanation: Herodias used her daughter’s dance and Herod’s oath to demand John’s head.
common_misconception: Herod feared and even liked to hear John, yet still yielded.

question: What did the disciples think when they saw Jesus walking on the sea?
answer_choice_2: That He was a ghost
correct_answer: That He was a ghost
learning_objective: Recall the disciples’ terror on the sea.
explanation: They cried out in fear; Jesus said, “Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid.”
common_misconception: Their hearts were hardened — they had not understood about the loaves.

question: What does sending the twelve out two by two with almost nothing teach?
answer_choice_2: Dependence on God and urgency in the mission
correct_answer: Dependence on God and urgency in the mission
learning_objective: Interpret the instructions for the mission of the twelve.
explanation: No bread, bag, or money — they were to trust God’s provision through those who received them.
common_misconception: The specific packing list expresses trust, not a permanent rule.

question: How does Psalm 23 echo through the feeding of the five thousand?
answer_choice_2: Jesus, the Shepherd, has the crowd recline on green grass and feeds them
correct_answer: Jesus, the Shepherd, has the crowd recline on green grass and feeds them
learning_objective: See Jesus as the shepherd of Psalm 23.
explanation: He saw sheep without a shepherd, made them lie down on green grass, and set a table in the wilderness.
common_misconception: The green grass detail is a deliberate shepherd-psalm echo, not scenery.

question: Why does Mark weave the bleeding woman’s story inside Jairus’s story?
answer_choice_1: To fill time while the girl died
answer_choice_2: To let each story of desperate faith interpret the other
correct_answer: To let each story of desperate faith interpret the other
explanation: Twelve years of illness, a twelve-year-old girl — two hopeless cases met by the same power through faith.
common_misconception: The interruption is literary design, not accident.

question: What does Mark hint by saying Jesus “meant to pass by them” on the sea?
answer_choice_2: A divine self-revelation, as God “passed by” Moses and Job
answer_choice_3: He did not see the boat
correct_answer: A divine self-revelation, as God “passed by” Moses and Job
learning_objective: Recognize the theophany language in the sea-walking.
explanation: “Passing by” is how Scripture describes God revealing His glory; Jesus says “It is I” — I AM.
common_misconception: The phrase is revelation language, not an intention to abandon them.

question: What did the Pharisees criticize the disciples for?
answer_choice_2: Eating with defiled, unwashed hands
correct_answer: Eating with defiled, unwashed hands
explanation: The issue was the tradition of the elders, not hygiene or God’s written law.
common_misconception: The dispute concerned human tradition elevated over God’s command.

question: What did Jesus say truly defiles a person?
answer_choice_2: What comes out of the heart
correct_answer: What comes out of the heart
explanation: Evil thoughts, deeds, and words proceed from within, from the heart.
common_misconception: Defilement is moral and internal, not ceremonial and external.

question: How many loaves fed the four thousand?
answer_choice_2: Seven
correct_answer: Seven
explanation: Seven loaves and a few small fish fed four thousand, with seven baskets left over.
common_misconception: This is a distinct event from the feeding of the five thousand.

question: Who did Peter declare Jesus to be at Caesarea Philippi?
answer_choice_2: Elijah
correct_answer: The Christ
explanation: Against the crowd’s guesses, Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
common_misconception: The confession is the Gospel’s hinge — identity confessed, mission still misunderstood.

question: Which prophecy did Jesus quote against honoring God with lips while hearts are far away?
answer_choice_2: Isaiah 29:13
correct_answer: Isaiah 29:13
explanation: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me” — worship can be hollow.
common_misconception: The target is hypocrisy, not liturgy itself.

question: What marked the Syrophoenician woman’s request?
answer_choice_2: Humble, persistent faith from a Gentile
correct_answer: Humble, persistent faith from a Gentile
explanation: Accepting even the “crumbs,” she trusted Jesus’ power — and her daughter was freed.
common_misconception: Jesus’ hard saying drew out her faith rather than dismissing her.

question: What did Jesus warn the disciples to beware of in the boat?
answer_choice_2: The leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod
correct_answer: The leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod
explanation: While the disciples fussed over bread, Jesus warned against spreading unbelief and hardness.
common_misconception: Leaven pictures pervasive influence, not literal bread.

question: What was unusual about the healing of the blind man at Bethsaida?
answer_choice_2: It happened in two stages
correct_answer: It happened in two stages
explanation: First the man saw people “like trees, walking,” then Jesus touched him again and he saw clearly.
common_misconception: The two stages are unique to Mark and deliberately placed.

question: How does the two-stage healing mirror the disciples?
answer_choice_2: They saw Jesus’ identity only partially — Messiah, but not yet the cross
correct_answer: They saw Jesus’ identity only partially — Messiah, but not yet the cross
learning_objective: Read the healing as a picture of dawning sight.
explanation: Peter confesses the Christ, then immediately rejects the cross — clear sight comes in stages.
common_misconception: Mark places the healing just before the confession on purpose.

question: What did Jesus begin to teach immediately after Peter’s confession?
answer_choice_2: That the Son of Man must suffer, be killed, and rise after three days
correct_answer: That the Son of Man must suffer, be killed, and rise after three days
learning_objective: Link the confession to the first passion prediction.
explanation: From this point Jesus plainly taught the necessity of His suffering and resurrection.
common_misconception: “Must” marks divine necessity, not tragic accident.

question: Why did Jesus say to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan”?
answer_choice_2: Peter was setting his mind on the things of man, opposing God’s plan of a suffering Messiah
correct_answer: Peter was setting his mind on the things of man, opposing God’s plan of a suffering Messiah
learning_objective: Understand the severity of Jesus’ rebuke.
explanation: Rejecting the cross repeated the wilderness temptation — a kingdom without suffering.
common_misconception: Peter meant well; that is exactly what made the temptation serious.

question: What does it mean to take up your cross and follow Jesus?
answer_choice_2: Self-denial and following Jesus in sacrificial obedience, even to death
correct_answer: Self-denial and following Jesus in sacrificial obedience, even to death
explanation: Whoever would save his life will lose it; the Servant’s path is the disciple’s path.
common_misconception: The cross was an instrument of death, not a metaphor for inconvenience.

question: Who appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration?
answer_choice_2: Moses and Elijah
correct_answer: Moses and Elijah
explanation: The Law and the Prophets — Moses and Elijah — talked with the transfigured Jesus.
common_misconception: Their presence testifies that Scripture points to Jesus.

question: What did the Father’s voice say at the Transfiguration?
answer_choice_1: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him”
answer_choice_2: “Behold the Lamb of God”
correct_answer: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him”
explanation: The cloud overshadowed them and the voice commanded them to listen to the Son.
common_misconception: “Listen to him” includes His hard words about the cross.

question: How did the rich man respond when Jesus told him to sell all and follow?
answer_choice_2: He went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions
correct_answer: He went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions
explanation: Jesus, loving him, exposed the one thing he lacked; wealth held his heart.
common_misconception: Jesus’ demand was diagnosis, not a universal command to poverty.

question: What did blind Bartimaeus cry out to Jesus?
answer_choice_2: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
correct_answer: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
explanation: Though blind, he saw who Jesus was — the Son of David — and would not be silenced.
common_misconception: His title for Jesus is a confession, not politeness.

question: What did the father of the possessed boy cry out?
answer_choice_2: “I believe; help my unbelief!”
answer_choice_4: “Why could we not cast it out?”
correct_answer: “I believe; help my unbelief!”
explanation: Jesus honored a father’s imperfect but real faith and healed his son.
common_misconception: Real faith can coexist with the struggle against doubt.

question: How must one receive the kingdom of God?
answer_choice_2: Like a child
correct_answer: Like a child
explanation: He was indignant when children were hindered — the kingdom is received, not earned.
common_misconception: Childlikeness means dependent trust, not immaturity.

question: What did James and John ask of Jesus?
answer_choice_2: To sit at His right and left in His glory
correct_answer: To sit at His right and left in His glory
explanation: On the road to the cross, they sought thrones; Jesus answered with the cup and the ransom.
common_misconception: The places at His right and left would be taken by crucified criminals.

question: According to Jesus, who is greatest in the kingdom?
answer_choice_2: The servant of all
correct_answer: The servant of all
learning_objective: State the kingdom’s measure of greatness.
explanation: “If anyone would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.”
common_misconception: Greatness is redefined, not abolished.

question: What is Mark 10:45’s summary of Jesus’ mission?
answer_choice_2: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many
correct_answer: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many
explanation: This verse crowns the servanthood teaching and interprets the cross before it happens.
common_misconception: The verse is a mission statement, not a proverb.

question: How does Isaiah 53 stand behind Mark 10:45?
answer_choice_2: The Servant bears the sin of many — a substitutionary death
correct_answer: The Servant bears the sin of many — a substitutionary death
learning_objective: Connect the ransom saying to the Suffering Servant.
explanation: “A ransom for many” echoes the Servant who was numbered with transgressors and bore the sin of many.
common_misconception: Jesus interpreted His own death through Isaiah 53.

question: Why could the disciples not cast out the spirit from the boy?
answer_choice_2: “This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer”
correct_answer: “This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer”
explanation: Past success had perhaps bred self-reliance; power flows from dependence on God.
common_misconception: The lesson is dependence, not a technique for exorcism.

question: How did Jesus ground His teaching on marriage?
answer_choice_2: In creation — God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh
answer_choice_4: In the practice of the patriarchs
correct_answer: In creation — God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh
explanation: Jesus went behind Moses’ concession to God’s design: “What God has joined together, let not man separate.”
common_misconception: Hardness of heart occasioned the concession; creation states the intent.

question: What did the crowds shout as Jesus entered Jerusalem?
answer_choice_2: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
correct_answer: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!”
explanation: The crowd spread cloaks and branches, hailing the coming kingdom of David.
common_misconception: Within the week, Jerusalem’s acclaim turned to rejection.

question: What did Jesus do in the temple courts?
answer_choice_2: Overturned the money-changers’ tables and drove out the sellers
correct_answer: Overturned the money-changers’ tables and drove out the sellers
explanation: “My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations” — but they had made it a den of robbers.
common_misconception: His act was prophetic judgment, not loss of temper.

question: Who denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed twice?
answer_choice_2: Thomas
correct_answer: Peter
explanation: As Jesus had foretold, Peter denied Him and broke down weeping.
common_misconception: The risen Jesus specifically restored Peter — “tell his disciples and Peter.”

question: Who was compelled to carry Jesus’ cross?
answer_choice_2: Simon of Cyrene
correct_answer: Simon of Cyrene
explanation: Simon, coming in from the country, carried the cross behind Jesus.
common_misconception: Mark names his sons — likely known to his first readers.

question: Why did Jesus commend the poor widow’s offering?
answer_choice_2: Out of her poverty she gave everything she had
correct_answer: Out of her poverty she gave everything she had
explanation: Two small coins outweighed great sums, because she gave her whole living.
common_misconception: God measures the cost to the giver, not the amount.

question: What is the greatest commandment according to Jesus?
answer_choice_2: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength
correct_answer: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and strength
explanation: Jesus joined Deuteronomy 6:4-5 with Leviticus 19:18 — love God and neighbor.
common_misconception: The second commandment is like it but not identical to it.

question: What happened in the temple when Jesus died?
answer_choice_2: The curtain was torn in two, from top to bottom
correct_answer: The curtain was torn in two, from top to bottom
learning_objective: Recall the sign at Jesus’ death.
explanation: Torn from top to bottom — God’s act opening the way into His presence.
common_misconception: The direction of the tear signals divine action.

question: Who said, “Truly this man was the Son of God”?
answer_choice_2: The centurion facing the cross
correct_answer: The centurion facing the cross
learning_objective: Recall the confession at the cross.
explanation: A Gentile executioner spoke the confession Mark’s Gospel opened with.
common_misconception: Mark 1:1’s title is finally confessed by a human — at the cross.

question: What did Jesus pray in Gethsemane?
answer_choice_2: “Abba, Father… remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will”
answer_choice_4: “Into your hands I commit my spirit”
correct_answer: “Abba, Father… remove this cup from me. Yet not what I will, but what you will”
explanation: Greatly distressed, the Son entrusted Himself to the Father’s will — and drank the cup.
common_misconception: The “cup” is God’s judgment, which He willingly took.

question: Which psalm did Jesus quote from the cross?
answer_choice_2: Psalm 22 — “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
correct_answer: Psalm 22 — “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
learning_objective: Hear the cry of dereliction in its psalm.
explanation: The psalm of the righteous sufferer — mocked, pierced, garments divided — ends in vindication.
common_misconception: Quoting its first line invokes the whole psalm, including its hope.

question: How did Jesus answer the high priest’s question, “Are you the Christ?”
answer_choice_2: “I am, and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven”
answer_choice_4: “My kingdom is not of this world”
correct_answer: “I am, and you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power, coming with the clouds of heaven”
explanation: At the moment it cost His life, Jesus joined Daniel 7 and Psalm 110 to declare His identity.
common_misconception: The “blasphemy” verdict shows they understood the claim exactly.

question: What did the young man at the tomb tell the women?
answer_choice_2: “He has risen; he is not here… tell his disciples and Peter”
correct_answer: “He has risen; he is not here… tell his disciples and Peter”
explanation: The crucified Jesus is risen and goes before them to Galilee, as He said.
common_misconception: “And Peter” — the denier is singled out for restoration.

quiz_title: Week 21 — Mark 10:45 & Luke 1:1–4 (From Servant to Savior)
question: According to Mark 10:45, why did the Son of Man come?
answer_choice_1: To be served by the nations
answer_choice_2: To serve and to give his life as a ransom for many
correct_answer: To serve and to give his life as a ransom for many
explanation: The verse gathers Mark’s whole portrait: the Servant-King who dies to redeem.
common_misconception: Service and sacrifice define His mission, not power.

quiz_title: Week 21 — Mark 10:45 & Luke 1:1–4 (From Servant to Savior)
question: To whom does Luke address his Gospel?
answer_choice_2: Theophilus
correct_answer: Theophilus
explanation: Luke writes to “most excellent Theophilus,” likely a patron or official.
common_misconception: The name means “lover of God” — but he was a real recipient.

quiz_title: Week 21 — Mark 10:45 & Luke 1:1–4 (From Servant to Savior)
question: What did Luke say he did before writing his account?
answer_choice_2: Followed all things closely for some time past
correct_answer: Followed all things closely for some time past
learning_objective: Recall Luke’s claim of careful research.
explanation: Luke investigated carefully to write an orderly account.
common_misconception: Inspiration worked through research, not apart from it.

quiz_title: Week 21 — Mark 10:45 & Luke 1:1–4 (From Servant to Savior)
question: Whose testimony does Luke say his account rests on?
answer_choice_2: Eyewitnesses and ministers of the word
correct_answer: Eyewitnesses and ministers of the word
explanation: Those who saw from the beginning delivered these things to the church.
